title: A-B pair at separation 2, at rest: effective K_A(B) = 7.59 and K_B(A) = 10.59 at P = 2.5 (T <= 0.8)

claims.statement: One A and one B particle at rest, initial separation in [1.95, 2.05], duration at most 0.8: A accelerates toward B with magnitude K_A(B) / r^2.5 and B toward A with K_B(A) / r^2.5 (r the current separation), with K_A(B) = 7.59 and K_B(A) = 10.59 held constant. These are effective constants for this separation band and this time window; the claim makes no statement about other separations, longer times or the exponent. Over the window the separation falls from about 2 to about 0.45 (still falling at T = 0.8), so the claim covers the constant-K approach down to about 0.5. The ratio K_B(A)/K_A(B) = 1.40 is a property of these two runs only. Fitted to two lab-b runs (horizontal and vertical orientations; K values agree to 0.5 percent and the fits are at chi2/n about 1). Out-of-sample error at the tracker noise floor.
